newsitem.title: UK: British-U.S. open skies talks to resume Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: British-U.S. open skies talks to resume Tuesday.

text.p: Talks between the British and U.S. governments on an open skies pact to free the transatlantic airline market will resume tomorrow in Washington, Britain's Department of Transport (DoT) said on Monday.

A DoT official said the talks were scheduled for February 18 through February 20. Negotiating teams from both governments and representatives from the leading transatlantic airlines would attend, the official said.
Airline sources said the talks were likely to make progress on minor issues but said a major breakthrough or open skies agreement was unlikely.
British Airways Plc, whose proposed alliance with American Airlines is conditional on an open skies pact being clinched, said it still expected a deal to be reached.

'We are hopeful that the two governments will continue to make progress towards an open skies agreement and we believe negotiations can be successfully completed quite quickly,' a spokesman for British Airways said.
The last round of talks on open skies was postponed because a senior British government negotiator fell ill.

A number of hurdles need to be cleared before an open skies deal can be reached. The British government wants to link the open skies talks with the BA/AA alliance while the U.S. wants to keep the talks and alliance approval as two distinct issues.
